avoid_when: Most useful information is in the ordered item sequence rather than tabular field interactions.
Feature dimensions or categorical vocabularies are so sparse that extra cross capacity overfits despite regularization.
candidates.summary: Augment an embedding-plus-MLP scorer with a small Deep & Cross Network branch so that user, video, context, popularity, and history fields receive explicit bounded-degree crosses alongside nonlinear deep interactions.
candidates.title: Deep & Cross ranker for bounded-order feature interactions
use_when: Interactions such as user-by-category affinity, video-by-context, and recency-by-history-length are expected to matter.
You want controlled explicit crosses without enumerating manual feature conjunctions.
The embedding-plus-MLP baseline has useful signal but leaves room for better GAUC or nDCG@5.

avoid_when: Using calibration metrics as a replacement for GAUC or nDCG@5 model selection
Fitting a calibrator on validation labels and then reporting that same validation result
Applying monotonic calibration solely to manufacture a ranking gain
candidates.summary: Supplement rank metrics with train-fitted calibration diagnostics such as Brier score, log loss, reliability bins, and predicted-positive-rate checks. Inspect errors separately for mixed candidate groups, because a model can preserve ranking while producing unstable probabilities that impair multitask weighting, threshold analyses, and ensemble averaging.
candidates.title: Probability calibration and ranking-error audit
use_when: Training with BCE or multitask binary heads
Averaging predictions or combining score heads
Investigating whether a ranking improvement came with implausibly extreme or collapsed probabilities

avoid_when: The baseline is underfit or training is already compute-constrained.
Perturbation strength has not been bounded relative to typical embedding norms.
Using a highly brittle listwise implementation that cannot safely perform a second forward/backward pass.
candidates.summary: Add a small worst-case norm-bounded perturbation to learned user, video, and optional metadata embeddings during training, then optimize the ordinary ranking loss plus the perturbed-loss term. Start from a converged non-adversarial checkpoint and perturb only dense embedding representations, not raw IDs or causal aggregate inputs.
candidates.title: Adversarial perturbation regularization for embedding rankers
use_when: Embedding-based rankers overfit despite ordinary dropout and weight decay.
Validation performance is unstable across seeds or degrades sharply for sparse entities.
A robust regularization experiment is justified after a strong baseline exists.

avoid_when: never replace fixed evaluation
candidates.summary: Explains official and advisory metrics, their weighting, tradeoffs, and interpretation hazards.
candidates.title: Within-user ranking and diagnostic metrics
use_when: diagnosing every scored experiment
predicting metric-specific effects

avoid_when: The target is driven mainly by stable user-video affinity and histories are mostly sparse.
Event timestamps are tied or unreliable enough that causal ordering cannot be implemented safely.
Scarce experiment budget cannot support checking sequence length, dropout, and attention-width sensitivity.
candidates.summary: Encode each user's strictly pre-impression video sequence with a lightweight causal self-attention encoder, combine its last-state representation with the candidate video and context embeddings, and score the displayed impression with a shallow head.
candidates.title: Causal self-attentive sequence encoder ranker
use_when: Timestamp ordering is reliable and sequential transitions or evolving interests are likely to add signal beyond aggregates.
Users have enough prior interactions for sequence modeling after causal truncation.
You can cap history length and use a small transformer to keep training and inference practical.

avoid_when: Searching many unplanned slices until a favorable result appears
Ranking models by tiny slices with inadequate mixed-label groups
Using slices built from post-impression information unavailable at scoring time
candidates.summary: Decompose validation GAUC and nDCG@5 into predeclared slices: validation time block, user-history depth, user and video frequency bucket, candidate-group size, and zero-positive, mixed, or all-positive label composition. Report support and uncertainty beside each slice rather than selecting models from a single noisy subgroup.
candidates.title: Temporal and population-slice ranking dashboard
use_when: Checking whether an overall gain is robust across late validation time blocks
Diagnosing cold or sparse-entity failures
Selecting between models with similar aggregate metrics but different deployment risks

avoid_when: The validation result shows that a candidate-specific reading of behavioral history is consistently valuable.
A simple model already saturates both GAUC and nDCG@5 and scarce experiments are better spent on objective or feature changes.
candidates.summary: A compact pointwise scorer that concatenates user/video ID embeddings, metadata embeddings, causal history features, and numeric aggregates before a residual MLP outputs one long-view logit per impression.
candidates.title: Embedding-plus-MLP pointwise ranker
use_when: A strong, low-risk architecture baseline is needed before adding specialized interaction or sequence modules.
Candidate lists are short and scoring every displayed impression independently is computationally inexpensive.
You need an architecture that cleanly accommodates all causally available dense and categorical features.

avoid_when: Training has clear late-epoch divergence or abrupt learning-rate restarts.
Batch-normalization statistics or incompatible optimizer/model states make direct averaging unsafe.
The checkpoint window would be chosen after inspecting many unrelated validation variants.
candidates.summary: Save checkpoints at predetermined epochs, select a small contiguous late-training window using the primary validation composite, and average compatible model weights before emitting the canonical prediction artifact. Use the exact same checkpoint schedule and one predeclared tie rule across experiments to reduce variance without repeatedly searching validation noise.
candidates.title: Validation-safe metric-aligned checkpoint averaging
use_when: Training curves are noisy across late epochs.
The model uses a stable optimizer trajectory and identical parameter shapes across checkpoints.
Experiment IDs are scarce and an inexpensive robustness improvement is preferable to broad hyperparameter sweeps.

avoid_when: Aggregate tables include the target row, future events, or validation/test outcomes.
Counts are treated as static when they are unavailable at the actual impression time.
The supplied aggregate-statistics table has unclear causal provenance.
required_features: video attributes or creator fields; use none when unavailable
candidates.summary: Add smoothed, causally available counts and rates for videos, creators or categories, plus user-by-attribute affinities, fitted on training prefixes and backed off for sparse groups.
candidates.title: Train-prefix smoothed popularity and affinity statistics
use_when: IDs and metadata are sparse enough that aggregate evidence can complement embeddings.
The pipeline can enforce train-only fitting and timestamp-prefix lookup.
Rare-item estimates can be shrunk toward global or attribute-level priors.

avoid_when: Training a strictly pointwise-only baseline where group reconstruction materially limits throughput.
Candidate-group identifiers cannot be reconstructed reliably.
required_features: candidate order or stable impression identifier
candidates.summary: Build minibatches from complete displayed candidate groups rather than independent impressions. Stratify group sampling by zero-positive, mixed-label, and all-positive groups, while ensuring every mixed group retains all of its displayed candidates so pairwise and listwise losses see valid within-user comparisons.
candidates.title: Group-complete, label-stratified minibatching
use_when: Training RankNet, LambdaRank-style, or ListNet objectives.
The primary metrics are computed within user candidate groups.
Mixed-label groups are uncommon enough that ordinary row sampling yields many uninformative batches.

avoid_when: Running a broad exploratory sweep with plentiful inexpensive local compute.
The candidate changes are inseparable because they must be introduced jointly for the method to function.
required_features: experiment ledger with parent run ID
candidates.summary: Organize experiments as a short ordered ladder of falsifiable changes from a fixed reference model. Before training, record the expected metric direction, one primary mechanism, required resources, acceptance margin, and rollback rule for each change. Advance only when the preceding change clears its predeclared confirmation criterion; otherwise retain the parent configuration and redirect the next experiment toward a genuinely different failure mode.
candidates.title: Predeclared hypothesis ladder with stop and rollback rules
use_when: Official experiment IDs are scarce and each submitted run must have a clear purpose.
Several plausible architecture, feature, objective, or training changes compete for a limited budget.
The team needs an auditable reason for why a configuration was promoted or abandoned.

avoid_when: Propensities are unavailable, estimated from post-impression variables, or have severe non-overlap.
The random-exposure sample is too small to substantiate an exposure-bias motivation.
Training becomes unstable after predeclared clipping and normalization; retain the unweighted baseline rather than repeatedly tuning clipping thresholds.
required_features: pre-impression covariates used to estimate propensity when propensities are not logged
candidates.summary: Replace the ordinary contribution of each observed long-view label with a stabilized clipped inverse-exposure-propensity weight, then optimize weighted BCE or weighted positive-negative RankNet pairs only within complete displayed candidate groups. Normalize weights within minibatches and cap both individual and group total weight so rare-propensity examples improve exposure robustness without dominating the ranking signal.
candidates.title: Clipped IPS-weighted within-group ranking loss
use_when: The propensity-overlap gate passes and exposure probabilities describe the data-generating display mechanism.
A strong unweighted BCE or RankNet baseline is already available for a one-variable comparison.
The expected bias concerns are primarily position, presentation, or selective-exposure bias rather than label-definition error.

avoid_when: Only one prediction artifact is available for either model.
Candidate groups cannot be reconstructed reliably from validation rows.
The comparison changes data, labels, or validation membership rather than only the model configuration.
required_features: seed identifiers and deterministic bootstrap seed
candidates.summary: Treat promotion as a paired comparison between a challenger and its parent using their predictions on the identical frozen validation rows. Resample complete displayed candidate groups, recompute the composite plus GAUC and nDCG@5 deltas, and report confidence intervals and win probability. For changes likely to be seed-sensitive, require confirmation across a small fixed set of seeds and promote only if the mean gain clears a predeclared practical margin without a material component-metric regression.
candidates.title: Paired group-bootstrap and multi-seed promotion test
use_when: Observed improvements are small relative to expected training and candidate-group variance.
A new objective, sequence model, or regularizer may have unstable optimization.
Two models produce predictions on exactly the same validation candidate groups.

avoid_when: The official split is effectively i.i.d. or temporal analysis shows no material drift.
The recent period is too small or label-sparse to support stronger weighting.
Timestamps, event ordering, or cutoff handling are ambiguous and could introduce future information.
candidates.summary: Apply a bounded exponential time-decay multiplier to complete training candidate groups, preserving within-group labels and user normalization while giving recent impressions more influence. Select only from a short predeclared half-life grid, normalize total training weight, and retain a nonzero minimum weight for older groups so the ranker adapts to preference or inventory drift without catastrophically forgetting sparse entities.
candidates.title: Recency-weighted causal ranking training
use_when: Chronological validation or the temporal slice dashboard indicates recent-period ranking degradation.
Timestamps are reliable and all recency weights are computed relative to the training cutoff, never future validation data.
The catalog, popularity distribution, or engagement behavior plausibly changes over the observation window.

avoid_when: Components are tightly coupled and invalid or meaningless in isolation.
The reference implementation is not yet deterministic enough for controlled comparisons.
The budget cannot support even a minimal baseline-plus-ablation block.
required_features: fixed training seed or seed block
candidates.summary: Anchor all experiments to one reproducible reference ranker, then test a compact orthogonal set of high-value interventions such as causal history, aggregate features, ranking loss, and auxiliary supervision. Use a fractional-factorial or staged add-remove design to estimate main effects first, reserve only a small number of runs for interactions suggested by shared mechanisms, and retain the same seed, budget, feature availability policy, and checkpoint rule within each comparison block.
candidates.title: Anchored fractional-factorial ablation plan
use_when: Several proposed improvements overlap and naive sequential additions would obscure attribution.
The project needs to identify which components merit combination.
Feature and objective changes can be toggled independently from a common backbone.

avoid_when: Creating an auxiliary retrieval benchmark explicitly defined over a different full-catalog candidate universe
Treating sampled-negative metrics as interchangeable with the fixed official ranking metric
candidates.summary: Evaluate every model on the exact supplied displayed candidate groups and their canonical row order. Audit group completeness, duplicate rows, score coverage, label composition, and denominator handling before metric computation; never replace displayed candidates with sampled negatives for the official result.
candidates.title: Frozen displayed-candidate evaluation audit
use_when: Implementing official within-user GAUC or nDCG@5 scoring
Validating a newly generated prediction artifact
Comparing models whose dataloaders or ranking heads may reorder, drop, or duplicate impressions

avoid_when: Neither propensity nor outcome nuisance models can be validated independently.
The random-exposure data has negligible coverage of important users, videos, or contexts, making nuisance-model extrapolation dominant.
Implementation cannot enforce fold separation or train-only fitting for imputation and propensity models.
required_features: exposure propensity or train-fitted propensity estimate
imputation-model inputs restricted to impression-time availability
fold or temporal split identifier for nuisance-model isolation
candidates.summary: Combine a direct long-view outcome model with a propensity-corrected residual loss: train the ranking model on an imputed outcome term plus a clipped IPS correction for observed-label errors. Cross-fit or isolate nuisance-model fitting from scored folds, keep the final scorer group-aware, and compare against both ordinary and IPS-only objectives to determine whether the imputation model reduces high-variance propensity correction.
candidates.title: Doubly robust exposure-debiased ranking objective
use_when: Propensities pass overlap checks but IPS-only training is noisy or sensitive to reasonable clipping levels.
There is adequate training support to fit both an outcome/imputation model and a propensity model using only pre-impression information.
The experiment budget supports a clearly predeclared three-way test: ordinary baseline, IPS, and doubly robust.

avoid_when: Candidate models are highly correlated checkpoint or seed variants with no complementary errors.
The ensemble weights would require extensive adaptive tuning on the frozen validation set.
One component has invalid, missing, nonfinite, or differently ordered predictions.
candidates.summary: Construct a small final ensemble only from independently useful finalists whose validation score residuals are not nearly identical. Convert each model's scores to within-candidate-group ranks or standardized groupwise scores before averaging, use fixed equal weights or one predeclared coarse weight grid, and require the ensemble to improve the parent models under paired group bootstrap. Prefer diversity across inductive biases, such as dot-product, cross-feature, and sequence-history scorers, rather than ensembling minor hyperparameter variants of one model.
candidates.title: Diversity-gated rank ensemble decision
use_when: Several validated models have complementary GAUC and nDCG@5 error patterns.
Prediction artifacts are available in the exact canonical validation order.
A final inference-time increase is acceptable and component models can be reproduced.
